questions.stem: A 3-month-old boy is evaluated for failure to thrive and lethargy. A CBC shows a macrocytic anemia that does not improve after several weeks of vitamin B12 and folate supplementation. His parents note a chalky, powdery residue in his diapers. Urinalysis reveals markedly elevated orotic acid, and serum ammonia is normal. Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is the most likely cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenosine deaminase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ornithine transcarbamoylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uridine monophosphate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine oxidase

explanation.summary: Hereditary orotic aciduria results from a deficiency of UMP synthase, producing macrocytic anemia and orotic aciduria without hyperammonemia.
explanation.whyCorrect: UMP synthase (UMPS) converts orotic acid into UMP, the precursor of all pyrimidines. When it is deficient, orotic acid accumulates and is excreted (the powdery diaper residue), and impaired pyrimidine/DNA synthesis causes a macrocytic anemia that is unresponsive to B12 and folate. Normal ammonia distinguishes it from the urea-cycle cause of orotic aciduria.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenosine deaminase deficiency disrupts purine catabolism and causes SCID with loss of B and T cells, not macrocytic anemia with orotic aciduria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan) impairs purine salvage, causing severe gout, self-mutilation, and neurologic findings, not orotic aciduria or anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ornithine transcarbamoylase deficiency also raises orotic acid but produces hyperammonemia and no anemia; this infant has normal ammonia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase acts in purine degradation to form uric acid; its inhibition lowers uric acid and is unrelated to pyrimidine synthesis or this presentation.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 4-month-old girl is diagnosed with hereditary orotic aciduria after presenting with a macrocytic anemia unresponsive to B12 and folate along with elevated urinary orotic acid. Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term treatment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Allopurinol

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation

choices.label: C
choices.text: High-dose folate and vitamin B12

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low-purine diet

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uridine supplementation

explanation.summary: Uridine (or UMP) supplementation bypasses the UMPS block and restores pyrimidine production.
explanation.whyCorrect: In hereditary orotic aciduria the block is at UMP synthase. Administering uridine provides UMP downstream of the deficient enzyme, restoring synthesis of all other pyrimidines and correcting the DNA synthesis defect and anemia. This is a lifelong therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase to lower uric acid in gout; it has no role in pyrimidine synthesis or this anemia.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Stem cell transplant is used for the immune failure of ADA-SCID, not for a pyrimidine biosynthetic enzyme deficiency correctable with uridine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The anemia is caused by an enzymatic block, not a vitamin deficiency, and is explicitly unresponsive to folate and B12.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A low-purine diet targets uric acid production in gout and does not address the pyrimidine synthesis defect.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 3-day-old neonate develops lethargy, poor feeding, vomiting, and tachypnea. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated serum ammonia and increased urinary orotic acid, but hemoglobin and MCV are normal. Deficiency of which of the following enzymes best explains these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenosine deaminase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ornithine transcarbamoylase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ribonucleotide reductase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uridine monophosphate synthase

explanation.summary: OTC deficiency causes orotic aciduria WITH hyperammonemia and no anemia, distinguishing it from hereditary orotic aciduria.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ornithine transcarbamoylase acts in the urea cycle just after CPSI. Its deficiency causes carbamoyl phosphate to accumulate and spill into the pyrimidine de novo pathway, raising orotic acid, while loss of urea cycle function produces hyperammonemia. Unlike hereditary orotic aciduria, there is no anemia.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes SCID from disrupted purine catabolism, not hyperammonemia with orotic aciduria.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CPSII is the cytoplasmic pyrimidine enzyme; its loss would decrease pyrimidine synthesis, not cause carbamoyl phosphate spillover, hyperammonemia, or elevated orotic acid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribonucleotide reductase makes deoxyribonucleotides and is unrelated to ammonia handling or orotic acid accumulation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UMPS deficiency causes orotic aciduria with macrocytic anemia and normal ammonia, whereas this infant has hyperammonemia and normal blood counts.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 48-year-old man undergoing radiation therapy for a rapidly shrinking tumor awakens with excruciating pain in his right great toe. The metatarsophalangeal joint of the hallux is swollen, red, warm, and exquisitely tender. His acute presentation is caused by overproduction of the end product of which of the following pathways?

choices.label: A
choices.text: De novo purine synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: De novo pyrimidine synthesis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purine degradation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Purine salvage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyrimidine degradation

explanation.summary: Massive cell turnover releases purines that are catabolized to uric acid, precipitating a gout flare.
explanation.whyCorrect: Rapid destruction of tumor cells liberates large amounts of purines that flux into the catabolic pathway, and the end product uric acid forms sodium urate crystals in the joint. Gout classically presents with rapid onset in the MTP joint of the hallux, exactly as described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Gout results from purine breakdown (degradation), not from de novo synthesis of purines.
whyWrongByChoice.B: De novo pyrimidine synthesis yields UMP and other pyrimidines, not uric acid, and its excess does not cause gout.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Purine salvage recycles bases into nucleotides and does not overproduce uric acid.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimidine degradation products are highly water soluble and cause no known human disease.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with recurrent gout flares is started on allopurinol for long-term management. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Blocks glutamine PRPP amidotransferase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Covalently inhibits xanthine oxidase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increases renal excretion of uric acid

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Inhibits microtubule polymerization in neutrophils

explanation.summary: Allopurinol is a purine analogue that inhibits xanthine oxidase, lowering uric acid synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Allopurinol is a well-tolerated free purine analogue that covalently binds the active site of xanthine oxidase, the enzyme that converts hypoxanthine and guanine into uric acid. Blocking it decreases uric acid production and is used for chronic gout control.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glutamine PRPP amidotransferase is inhibited by the 6-mercaptopurine metabolite TIMP, not by allopurinol.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increasing uric acid excretion (uricosuric action) describes probenecid, not allopurinol.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibition describes methotrexate, which limits the folate pool.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Inhibiting microtubule polymerization describes colchicine, which blunts crystal phagocytosis in acute flares.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman presents with an acute, intensely painful, swollen first toe joint. Joint aspiration shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. She is given colchicine for the acute attack. Which of the following best explains how colchicine relieves her symptoms?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It dissolves sodium urate crystals directly

choices.label: B
choices.text: It increases uric acid excretion in the urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: It inhibits microtubule polymerization

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits PRPP synthetase to reduce purine production

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits xanthine oxidase, lowering uric acid

explanation.summary: Colchicine inhibits microtubule polymerization, blocking neutrophil phagocytosis of urate crystals and the resulting inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Engulfment of sodium urate crystals by phagocytes drives cell damage and release of inflammatory mediators. Colchicine inhibits microtubule polymerization, preventing phagocytosis of the crystals and thereby attenuating the inflammatory response during an acute flare.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Colchicine does not chemically dissolve existing urate crystals; it blocks the inflammatory response to them.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Increasing uric acid excretion is the uricosuric action of probenecid.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PRPP synthetase is not a target of colchicine, and its inhibition is not how acute gout inflammation is controlled.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase inhibition is the mechanism of allopurinol, a preventive agent, not colchicine.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has intellectual disability, dystonia, and compulsive self-mutilation with bitten lips and fingers. Laboratory studies show markedly elevated uric acid, and he has had gout-like attacks. His disorder arises from a defect in an enzyme of which of the following processes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: De novo pyrimidine synthesis

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deoxyribonucleotide formation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Purine salvage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyrimidine salvage

choices.label: E
choices.text: Urea cycle

explanation.summary: Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is an HGPRT deficiency in the purine salvage pathway.
explanation.whyCorrect: Lesch-Nyhan results from deficiency of HGPRT, the major purine salvage enzyme. Without salvage, purines are shunted to uric acid and de novo synthesis loses feedback regulation, causing severe hyperuricemia/gout plus the characteristic neurologic impairment and self-mutilating behavior.

whyWrongByChoice.A: De novo pyrimidine synthesis defects (e.g., UMPS) cause orotic aciduria and macrocytic anemia, not hyperuricemia with self-mutilation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Ribonucleotide reductase makes deoxyribonucleotides and is unrelated to this salvage-pathway disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyrimidine salvage disorders are not associated with elevated uric acid or the neurobehavioral features of Lesch-Nyhan.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A urea cycle defect such as OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia, not this purine/uric acid syndrome.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 6-month-old infant has had recurrent severe opportunistic infections since birth. Immunologic workup reveals a profound deficiency of both B and T lymphocytes. The responsible enzyme normally catalyzes which of the following reactions in nucleotide metabolism?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Addition of a methyl group to dUMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of orotic acid to UMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deamination of AMP to inosine monophosphate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Formation of PRPP from ribose 5-phosphate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduction of the 2' carbon of ribose

explanation.summary: ADA deficiency causes SCID; adenosine deaminase normally deaminates AMP/adenosine to IMP for degradation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes a form of SCID (about 10-20% of cases) with loss of B and T cells. AMP is unique in that it must first be deaminated by ADA to form IMP before it can enter the common purine degradation pathway; loss of ADA disrupts nucleotide recycling and is toxic to lymphocytes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Methylating dUMP is the thymidylate synthase reaction, unrelated to SCID.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Conversion of orotic acid to UMP is done by UMP synthase; its deficiency causes hereditary orotic aciduria, not SCID.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PRPP formation is catalyzed by PRPP synthetase and is not the immunodeficiency-causing enzyme here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reducing the 2' carbon of ribose is the ribonucleotide reductase reaction, not the enzyme deficient in ADA-SCID.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: In the de novo purine synthesis pathway, one enzyme constitutes the committed, most heavily regulated step: it is activated by PRPP and inhibited by the downstream products AMP, GMP, and IMP. Which of the following is this enzyme?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glutamine PRPP amidotransferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: D
choices.text: PRPP synthetase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine oxidase

explanation.summary: Glutamine PRPP amidotransferase is the committed, regulated step of de novo purine synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: This enzyme catalyzes the transfer of a nitrogen from glutamine onto carbon 1 of PRPP and is the committed step. It is feed-forward activated by PRPP and feedback inhibited by the end products AMP, GMP, and IMP, matching the description.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CPSII is the regulated step of pyrimidine, not purine, de novo synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HGPRT is a purine salvage enzyme, not the committed de novo synthesis step.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PRPP synthetase makes PRPP but is explicitly NOT the committed step, since PRPP has many fates beyond purine synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase functions in purine degradation to uric acid, not in de novo synthesis regulation.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A rapidly dividing cell must generate deoxyribonucleotide substrates for DNA replication. Which of the following enzymes accomplishes this by reducing the 2' carbon of the ribose sugar, using reducing power ultimately supplied by NADPH via thioredoxin?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)

choices.label: B
choices.text: PRPP synthetase (PRPS1)

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ribonucleotide reductase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase (TYMS)

choices.label: E
choices.text: UMP synthase (UMPS)

explanation.summary: Ribonucleotide reductase converts ribonucleotides to deoxyribonucleotides by reducing the ribose 2' carbon.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ribonucleotide reductase removes the 2' hydroxyl of the ribose sugar to produce the deoxyribose needed for DNA. The oxidation-reduction is powered by reduced thioredoxin, which is regenerated by thioredoxin reductase using NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway. All nucleotides pass through RR except dTMP, which comes from dUMP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dihydrofolate reductase regenerates FH4 from DHF and does not act on the sugar.
whyWrongByChoice.B: PRPP synthetase adds pyrophosphate to ribose 5-phosphate and does not reduce the 2' carbon.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase methylates dUMP to form dTMP; it does not reduce the ribose 2' carbon.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UMP synthase converts orotic acid to UMP in pyrimidine synthesis, not ribose reduction.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A patient with severe dietary folate deficiency is evaluated for impaired nucleotide synthesis. Because folate one-carbon donation is required for the synthesis of certain nucleotides but not others, production of which of the following nucleotides remains essentially unaffected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: AMP

choices.label: B
choices.text: dTMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: GMP

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)

choices.label: E
choices.text: UMP

explanation.summary: Folate (and B12) are required for dTMP, GMP, and AMP but not for CMP or UMP.
explanation.whyCorrect: The synthetic cascades show one-carbon folate donations are needed to make dTMP, GMP, and AMP, whereas UMP (and CMP) synthesis does not require folate. Thus in folate deficiency, UMP production is essentially unaltered even as the folate-dependent nucleotides fall.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMP is derived from IMP, whose purine ring requires folate one-carbon donations, so its production falls.
whyWrongByChoice.B: dTMP synthesis by thymidylate synthase directly consumes a folate one-carbon unit, so it is suppressed in folate deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.C: GMP is likewise derived from folate-dependent IMP synthesis and is decreased.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IMP formation requires multiple folate-dependent one-carbon donations, so it is impaired in folate deficiency.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A patient with leukemia is treated with 6-mercaptopurine, an inert purine analogue prodrug. When it is salvaged by HGPRT it is converted to thioinosine monophosphate (TIMP), which mediates the drug's antineoplastic effect. TIMP acts by inhibiting which of the following enzymes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glutamine PRPP amidotransferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ribonucleotide reductase (RNR)

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase (TYMS)

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine oxidase (xanthine dehydrogenase)

explanation.summary: The 6-mercaptopurine metabolite TIMP potently inhibits glutamine PRPP amidotransferase, blocking de novo purine synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: When 6-mercaptopurine is salvaged by HGPRT it forms TIMP, a potent inhibitor of glutamine PRPP amidotransferase and other purine de novo enzymes. This deprives rapidly growing cancer cells of the purine substrates needed for DNA synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Dihydrofolate reductase is the target of methotrexate, not TIMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ribonucleotide reductase is not the enzyme inhibited by the 6-mercaptopurine metabolite TIMP.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase is inhibited by the 5-fluorouracil metabolite FdUMP, not by TIMP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase is inhibited by allopurinol, and it metabolizes 6-MP to 6-thiouric acid rather than being a TIMP target.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A biochemistry student is asked to identify the nitrogenous base that is present in RNA but never found in DNA. Which of the following bases is the correct answer?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytosine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Guanine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uracil

explanation.summary: Uracil is the pyrimidine unique to RNA; thymine is the pyrimidine unique to DNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Five major nitrogenous bases make up nucleic acids. Adenine, guanine, and cytosine appear in both DNA and RNA, whereas thymine is a pyrimidine found in DNA only and uracil is a pyrimidine found in RNA only.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Adenine is a purine found in both DNA and RNA.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Cytosine is a pyrimidine found in both DNA and RNA.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Guanine is a purine found in both DNA and RNA.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymine is the pyrimidine that is present in DNA only, the reverse of what is asked.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A researcher isolates a nucleotide and wants to predict whether it will be incorporated into DNA or RNA. Which of the following structural features determines this?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Attachment of the base at the 1' pentose carbon

choices.label: B
choices.text: Number of phosphate groups attached at the 5' carbon

choices.label: C
choices.text: Presence of a hydroxyl group on the 2' pentose carbon

choices.label: D
choices.text: Presence of a hydroxyl group on the 3' pentose carbon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Single-ring versus double-ring nitrogenous base

explanation.summary: The pentose sugar determines DNA versus RNA incorporation: ribose has a 2' hydroxyl, deoxyribose does not.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pentose sugar is the scaffold for the phosphates and base and determines whether a nucleotide is incorporated into DNA or RNA. Ribose, identified by the hydroxyl group on the 2' carbon, is the sugar of RNA nucleotides, whereas deoxyribose, with no hydroxyl on the 2' carbon, is the pentose in DNA.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The base is attached at the 1' carbon in both ribose and deoxyribose nucleotides.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Nucleotides may carry 1-3 phosphates (mono, di, tri); the phosphate count does not decide DNA versus RNA incorporation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Both ribose and deoxyribose carry a 3' hydroxyl; it is the 2' position that differs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Purines and pyrimidines both appear in DNA and RNA, so ring number does not determine which nucleic acid the nucleotide enters.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome is seen in clinic. His parents ask whether he faces the same risk of opportunistic infections as a cousin who was diagnosed with adenosine deaminase deficiency. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He has a higher risk because elevated uric acid suppresses lymphocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: He has the same risk because both disorders disrupt purine salvage

choices.label: C
choices.text: He is at risk only during periods of active gout flares

choices.label: D
choices.text: He will lose B cells but retain T cells, unlike his cousin

choices.label: E
choices.text: His immune system is functional despite the defect in nucleotide recycling

explanation.summary: Lesch-Nyhan patients have a functional immune system, unlike ADA-deficient patients who develop SCID.
explanation.whyCorrect: Even though both HGPRT deficiency (Lesch-Nyhan) and ADA deficiency occur within nucleotide recycling, individuals with Lesch-Nyhan syndrome have a functional immune system. In contrast, ADA deficiency causes severe combined immunodeficiency with loss of both T and B cells and susceptibility to opportunistic infections.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Lesch-Nyhan causes severe hyperuricemia and gout, but the immune system remains functional.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Although both involve nucleotide recycling, only ADA deficiency produces immunodeficiency; Lesch-Nyhan does not.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gout flares are not associated with immunodeficiency in Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lesch-Nyhan does not cause loss of either lymphocyte population; ADA SCID causes loss of both B and T cells.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: Hepatocytes store excess glucose as glycogen and also perform conjugation reactions for detoxification. Which of the following nucleotides serves as the high-energy carrier of glucose for these processes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATP

choices.label: B
choices.text: cAMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: CTP

choices.label: D
choices.text: GTP

choices.label: E
choices.text: UDP

explanation.summary: UDP is the high-energy carrier of glucose in the liver for glycogen formation and detoxifying conjugation reactions.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nucleotides are far more than DNA and RNA substrates. UDP is a high-energy carrier of glucose in the liver used for glycogen formation and for conjugation reactions in detoxification, illustrating a non-nucleic-acid role of a pyrimidine nucleotide.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP is the predominant energy source for biological work, not the glucose carrier for glycogen synthesis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: cAMP is a cyclized purine nucleotide that acts as a second messenger in signaling cascades.
whyWrongByChoice.C: CTP is a pyrimidine nucleotide but is not described as the glucose carrier for glycogen formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: GTP is a purine nucleotide; the brick identifies UDP, not GTP, as the glucose carrier.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A student argues that PRPP synthetase should be considered the committed step of de novo purine synthesis because it consumes ATP and is inhibited by purine nucleotides. Which of the following best explains why it is NOT the committed step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PRPP also serves pyrimidine synthesis, salvage, and NAD+ formation

choices.label: B
choices.text: PRPP formation proceeds without any ATP investment

choices.label: C
choices.text: The enzyme is activated rather than inhibited by AMP and GMP

choices.label: D
choices.text: The enzyme is not inhibited by purine nucleotide end products

choices.label: E
choices.text: The purine ring is assembled before ribose is activated

explanation.summary: PRPP has many fates beyond purine synthesis, so its formation cannot be the committed step.
explanation.whyCorrect: PRPP is used in de novo synthesis of both purines and pyrimidines, in salvage of purines and pyrimidines, and in synthesis of NAD+ from tryptophan. Because PRPP has many fates aside from de novo purine synthesis, PRPP production by PRPP synthetase is not the committed step; that role belongs to glutamine PRPP amidotransferase.

whyWrongByChoice.B: PRPP formation requires an initial ATP investment to add pyrophosphate to ribose 5-phosphate.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Purine nucleotide end products inhibit, not activate, PRPP synthetase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: PRPP synthetase IS negatively inhibited by purine nucleotide end products; this is not why it fails to be the committed step.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The pyrophosphate activates the sugar so the purine ring is built on carbon 1 of PRPP, after activation.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man presents at 5 AM with 6 hours of excruciating pain, swelling, redness, and warmth of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint. He has had two similar episodes over the past year. Which of the following is the priority of initial therapy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increasing uric acid excretion with probenecid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lowering uric acid production with allopurinol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Managing pain and inflammation with an NSAID

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reducing nucleotide synthesis with methotrexate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restricting dietary purines from red meat and seafood

explanation.summary: In an acute gout flare, the initial priority is controlling pain and inflammation with medication such as NSAIDs.
explanation.whyCorrect: Engulfment of sodium urate crystals damages phagocytes and releases major inflammatory mediators. A priority in initial therapy is therefore to manage the pain and inflammation through medication such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; longer-term management uses combinations of allopurinol, colchicine, and probenecid.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Probenecid is a uricosuric used for management and is less prescribed; it is not the initial priority in a flare.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Allopurinol lowers uric acid production for ongoing management but does not address the acute pain and inflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and has no role in the initial therapy of gout.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A high-purine diet is a risk factor, but dietary change is not the initial therapy for an acute attack.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: During normal nucleotide turnover, free guanine is released and recycled by hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase. Which of the following is the direct product of this reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenosine monophosphate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Guanosine monophosphate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inosine monophosphate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uric acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine

explanation.summary: HGPRT adds hypoxanthine or guanine directly to PRPP to form IMP or GMP, respectively.
explanation.whyCorrect: HGPRT is the major purine salvage enzyme. It transfers either hypoxanthine or guanine onto PRPP; hypoxanthine yields IMP and guanine yields GMP. Salvage circumvents the ATP expense of de novo synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: AMP is formed by a separate enzyme, adenine phosphoribosyl transferase (APRT), from free adenine.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IMP is the HGPRT product when the substrate is hypoxanthine, not guanine.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uric acid is the product of purine degradation via xanthine oxidase, the opposite fate of salvage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine is not the product of salvage; salvage regenerates a nucleotide from the base.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A researcher studies a cell line with complete loss of HGPRT activity. Despite this, the cells continue to salvage one free purine base into a nucleotide using PRPP. Which of the following bases is still salvaged?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Guanine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypoxanthine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uracil

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine

explanation.summary: Adenine is salvaged by a separate enzyme, adenine phosphoribosyl transferase (APRT), independent of HGPRT.
explanation.whyCorrect: HGPRT handles hypoxanthine and guanine, but a separate enzyme, adenine phosphoribosyl transferase (APRT), reincorporates free adenine with PRPP to reform AMP. Loss of HGPRT therefore leaves adenine salvage intact.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Guanine salvage to GMP requires HGPRT and is lost in this cell line.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hypoxanthine salvage to IMP requires HGPRT and is lost in this cell line.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uracil is a pyrimidine, not a purine, and is salvaged by pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine is not described as a substrate of a purine salvage enzyme in this pathway.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A patient with leukemia is treated with 6-mercaptopurine. A portion of the administered drug is not salvaged by HGPRT but instead enters the purine degradation pathway. Which of the following products is formed from the drug by xanthine oxidase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 6-Thiouric acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inosine monophosphate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Thioinosine monophosphate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uric acid

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine

explanation.summary: 6-Mercaptopurine has two fates: xanthine oxidase converts it to 6-thiouric acid, while HGPRT salvage converts it to TIMP.
explanation.whyCorrect: 6-Mercaptopurine is an inert purine derivative prodrug. When it enters the purine degradation pathway it is converted to 6-thiouric acid via xanthine oxidase. Only the fraction salvaged by HGPRT becomes thioinosine monophosphate (TIMP), the active antineoplastic metabolite.

whyWrongByChoice.B: IMP is the normal purine intermediate; 6-MP is a thio-derivative and does not become IMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: TIMP is produced when 6-MP is salvaged by HGPRT, not when it is oxidized by xanthine oxidase.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Uric acid is the product of xanthine oxidase acting on native hypoxanthine and guanine, not on 6-MP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine is a native purine degradation intermediate, not the product formed from 6-MP.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II catalyzes the first step in UMP formation. Which of the following correctly pairs the activator and inhibitor of this enzyme?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activated by ATP, inhibited by orotic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text: Activated by glutamine, inhibited by UMP

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activated by PRPP, inhibited by AMP

choices.label: D
choices.text: Activated by PRPP, inhibited by UTP

choices.label: E
choices.text: Activated by UTP, inhibited by PRPP

explanation.summary: CPSII, the regulated step of de novo pyrimidine synthesis, is enhanced by PRPP and suppressed by UTP.
explanation.whyCorrect: CPSII produces carbamoyl phosphate from glutamine, CO2, and ATP as the first step in UMP formation. Its activity is enhanced by PRPP (feed-forward) and suppressed by UTP, a downstream pyrimidine end product, so that UMP formation is regulated at CPSII.

whyWrongByChoice.A: ATP is a substrate, not an allosteric activator, and orotic acid is an intermediate rather than the described inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glutamine is the nitrogen-donating substrate of CPSII, not its allosteric activator, and UTP rather than UMP is the described inhibitor.
whyWrongByChoice.C: AMP is a purine nucleotide that inhibits glutamine PRPP amidotransferase, not CPSII.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This reverses the true relationship: PRPP activates and UTP inhibits CPSII.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A student notes that carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I and carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II both generate carbamoyl phosphate, yet they are not classified as isozymes. Which of the following best explains this classification?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are both feedback-inhibited by the same end product

choices.label: B
choices.text: They differ only in their subcellular location within the cell

choices.label: C
choices.text: They function in the same pathway at different catalytic rates

choices.label: D
choices.text: They generate different products from an identical substrate

choices.label: E
choices.text: They obtain nitrogen from different substrates (ammonia versus glutamine)

explanation.summary: CPSI and CPSII make the same product but use different nitrogen substrates, so they are not isozymes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Carbamoyl phosphate is a common intermediate between the urea cycle (CPSI, mitochondria) and pyrimidine synthesis (CPSII, cytoplasm). Although the products are the same, CPSI obtains nitrogen from ammonia while CPSII uses glutamine. Because they use different substrates, they are not isozymes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CPSII is inhibited by UTP; a shared inhibitor is not described and would not explain non-isozyme status.
whyWrongByChoice.B: They do differ in location (mitochondria versus cytoplasm), but the stated basis for not being isozymes is their different substrates.
whyWrongByChoice.C: They serve different pathways, the urea cycle versus pyrimidine synthesis, not the same pathway.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The products are the same (carbamoyl phosphate); it is the nitrogen substrate that differs.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: Thymidylate synthase transfers a one-carbon unit from methylene-FH4 onto dUMP to generate dTMP. Which of the following amino acids typically supplies this one-carbon unit to tetrahydrofolate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspartate

choices.label: B
choices.text: Glutamine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Glycine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methionine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Serine

explanation.summary: Serine is the one-carbon amino acid donor that charges tetrahydrofolate for dTMP synthesis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Thymidine synthesis occurs after dUMP is produced by ribonucleotide reductase. Thymidylate synthase places a methyl group onto dUMP using methylene-FH4. Typically this one carbon is added to tetrahydrofolate from serine, the one-carbon amino acid donor, via serine hydroxymethyltransferase, which releases glycine.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Aspartate is not the one-carbon donor for methylene-FH4 formation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Glutamine donates nitrogen in purine and pyrimidine synthesis (e.g., to CPSII), not the one-carbon unit for dTMP.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Glycine is the product released by serine hydroxymethyltransferase after serine donates its carbon, not the donor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methionine is not described as the one-carbon donor to FH4 in this pathway.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A patient with cancer is treated with methotrexate. Within the folate cycle that supports dTMP production, which of the following enzymes is directly inhibited by this drug?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dihydrofolate reductase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ribonucleotide reductase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uridine monophosphate synthase

explanation.summary: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, preventing regeneration of FH4 from DHF.
explanation.whyCorrect: When thymidylate synthase transfers the methyl group from methylene-FH4 to dUMP, the folate is left as DHF. Dihydrofolate reductase regenerates FH4 from DHF so the cycle can continue. Methotrexate inhibits DHFR, limiting the folate pool and therefore dTMP production.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ribonucleotide reductase produces dUMP and other deoxyribonucleotides; it is not the methotrexate target.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase loads the one-carbon unit from serine onto FH4 and is not inhibited by methotrexate.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase is inhibited by FdUMP, the salvaged metabolite of 5-fluorouracil, not by methotrexate.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UMP synthase converts orotic acid to UMP in de novo pyrimidine synthesis and is not a methotrexate target.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman with severe, long-standing vitamin B12 and folate deficiency has a macrocytic anemia. In an experimental analysis of DNA base composition from her bone marrow cells, which of the following findings would most likely be observed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased proportion of adenine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased proportion of cytosine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased incorporation of uracil

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased proportion of guanine

choices.label: E
choices.text: Increased proportion of thymine

explanation.summary: When dTMP is limiting but UMP is not, cells attempting to replicate DNA substitute uracil, a base normally exclusive to RNA.
explanation.whyCorrect: Folate and B12 are required for dTMP but not for UMP or CMP synthesis. When dTMP is limiting, cells continue attempting to divide by nontraditional mechanisms, and DNA becomes enriched with uracil because UMP is still synthesized while dTMP is not. The cell replicates DNA at any cost, substituting a base usually exclusive to RNA; this is not a viable long-term solution.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The characteristic anomaly described is uracil enrichment, not a change in adenine proportion.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CMP synthesis does not require folate, and cytosine loss is not the described consequence.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Guanine is not described as increasing; the reported anomaly is uracil substitution for thymidine.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Thymine would be decreased, not increased, because dTMP synthesis depends on the folate pool.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: Because de novo synthesis of uracil nucleotides requires a significant ATP investment, cells recycle free uracil back into UMP. Which of the following enzymes catalyzes this salvage reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Adenine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uridine monophosphate synthase

explanation.summary: Pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase adds PRPP to uracil to reform UMP.
explanation.whyCorrect: Much like purines, pyrimidine salvage pathways exist because of the significant ATP investment needed to produce them from scratch. A key pyrimidine salvage enzyme is pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase, which adds PRPP to uracil, reforming UMP.

whyWrongByChoice.A: APRT salvages the purine adenine to reform AMP.
whyWrongByChoice.B: CPSII catalyzes the first de novo step, producing carbamoyl phosphate, and is not a salvage enzyme.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HGPRT salvages the purines hypoxanthine and guanine, not uracil.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UMPS is a de novo enzyme that converts orotic acid into UMP; it does not salvage free uracil.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 64-year-old man with colon cancer is started on 5-fluorouracil, a prodrug that must be converted to 5-fluorouracil monophosphate (FdUMP) to inhibit thymidylate synthase. Which of the following enzymes carries out this activation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytosine deaminase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymidylate synthase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xanthine oxidase

explanation.summary: 5-Fluorouracil is activated through the pyrimidine salvage pathway by pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase.
explanation.whyCorrect: Similar to 6-mercaptopurine, 5-fluorouracil is a prodrug activated through nucleotide salvage. As a pyrimidine derivative, it is converted to FdUMP by pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase. FdUMP then blocks thymidylate synthase, preventing dTMP production and DNA synthesis.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytosine deaminase converts fluorocytosine to fluorouracil; it is not needed to activate 5-fluorouracil itself.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HGPRT salvages purines and activates 6-mercaptopurine to TIMP; it does not act on a pyrimidine analogue.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Thymidylate synthase is the target inhibited by FdUMP, not the enzyme that activates 5-fluorouracil.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase acts in purine degradation and converts 6-MP to 6-thiouric acid, unrelated to 5-fluorouracil.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A patient with a fungal infection is treated with fluorocytosine. The drug is converted to FdUMP within the microbe but is relatively spared from activation in human cells. Which of the following best explains this selectivity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Human cells export the drug before it can be phosphorylated

choices.label: B
choices.text: Human cells lack the cytosine deaminase needed to convert it to fluorouracil

choices.label: C
choices.text: Human cells lack the pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase needed to salvage it

choices.label: D
choices.text: Human thymidylate synthase does not bind the fluorinated nucleotide

choices.label: E
choices.text: Microbial cells cannot degrade pyrimidines to water-soluble products

explanation.summary: Fluorocytosine must first be deaminated by cytosine deaminase, an enzyme many microbes express but humans lack.
explanation.whyCorrect: In contrast to 5-fluorouracil, fluorocytosine must first be deaminated before it can be salvaged. Cytosine deaminase removes the nitrogen from fluorocytosine to produce fluorouracil and eventually FdUMP. Humans lack cytosine deaminase, but many microbes express this enzyme, which provides the selectivity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Drug export is not the described mechanism; the difference lies in the deamination step.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Human cells do have pyrimidine phosphoribosyl transferase; that is how 5-fluorouracil itself is activated in patients.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Human thymidylate synthase is inhibited by FdUMP, which is why 5-fluorouracil works as a chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimidine degradation products are water soluble; this is irrelevant to fluorocytosine selectivity.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: Purine degradation is associated with gout, whereas pyrimidine degradation has no known associated human disease. Which of the following best explains this difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pyrimidine breakdown products are highly water soluble

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pyrimidine breakdown yields uric acid that is readily excreted

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pyrimidine catabolism is confined to the liver

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pyrimidines are never catabolized, only salvaged

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pyrimidines are too scarce in cells to accumulate

explanation.summary: Pyrimidine degradation products are highly water soluble, so they do not precipitate or cause disease.
explanation.whyCorrect: In contrast to purines, whose catabolism produces uric acid that can form sodium urate crystals, there are no known human diseases involving pyrimidine degradation because the products are highly water soluble.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Uric acid is the product of purine, not pyrimidine, degradation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Location of catabolism is not the described reason; solubility of the products is.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pyrimidines are degraded; the point is that their breakdown products cause no known disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimidines are abundant in nucleic acids; scarcity is not the explanation.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man with recurrent gout asks his physician whether testing should be done to determine if he overproduces uric acid or underexcretes it. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Distinguishing the two does not largely alter the course of treatment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Overproduction can only be confirmed by joint aspiration during a flare

choices.label: C
choices.text: Overproduction of uric acid accounts for the majority of gout cases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Underexcretion cases require a different set of first-line medications

choices.label: E
choices.text: Underexcretion is rare, occurring in about 10 percent of cases

explanation.summary: Most gout is from underexcretion (overproduction is only ~10%), and identifying which does not substantially change management.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gout results from either overproduction of uric acid, which accounts for only about 10% of cases, or underexcretion of uric acid. However, identifying which is occurring in a given patient does not largely benefit the physician or alter the course of treatment.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Joint aspiration identifies urate crystals to diagnose gout; it does not determine overproduction versus underexcretion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Overproduction accounts for only about 10% of cases; underexcretion is the majority.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The brick states that identifying the mechanism does not alter the course of treatment.
whyWrongByChoice.E: This reverses the numbers: overproduction, not underexcretion, occurs in about 10% of cases.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is awakened at 4 AM by severe pain in his right great toe that was normal when he went to bed. Which of the following best explains why gout attacks characteristically begin in the early morning in distal joints?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Daytime weight bearing damages the cartilage of distal joints

choices.label: B
choices.text: Immobility during sleep activates neutrophil phagocytosis

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lower temperature in distal joints reduces urate solubility

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overnight fasting accelerates de novo purine synthesis

choices.label: E
choices.text: Renal uric acid excretion rises during nighttime sleep

explanation.summary: Gout flares strike distal joints in the early morning because lower temperature lowers urate solubility, promoting crystal precipitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Gout attacks routinely occur in early morning hours after sleeping, are localized to a specific joint (most often the MTP joint of the hallux), and have rapid onset of less than 24 hours. The affected joints are typically distal, and the early morning onset is likely due to lower temperature impacting solubility of sodium urate.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cartilage damage from weight bearing is not the mechanism; crystal precipitation from reduced solubility is.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Phagocytosis of crystals follows precipitation; immobility is not described as its trigger.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nocturnal changes in de novo purine synthesis are not the described explanation for morning onset.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Increased renal excretion would lower, not raise, urate concentration and would not trigger a flare.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with chronic gout is prescribed a medication described as uricosuric. His physician notes that it is prescribed less often because of cost and the need for more frequent dosing. Which of the following drugs was most likely prescribed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 6-Mercaptopurine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allopurinol

choices.label: C
choices.text: Colchicine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Methotrexate

choices.label: E
choices.text: Probenecid

explanation.summary: Probenecid is the uricosuric gout drug that increases uric acid excretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Probenecid increases uric acid excretion, which is what defines a uricosuric drug. It is not as well prescribed as allopurinol due to cost and the need to take it more frequently.

whyWrongByChoice.A: 6-Mercaptopurine is an antineoplastic purine prodrug, not a uricosuric agent.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Allopurinol is a highly prescribed, well-tolerated purine analogue that inhibits xanthine oxidase; it lowers production rather than increasing excretion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Colchicine inhibits microtubule polymerization to prevent crystal phagocytosis; it has no uricosuric effect.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and is not a gout medication.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man who drinks several liters of soda sweetened with high fructose corn syrup each day develops recurrent gout flares. Which of the following best explains how this dietary habit promotes hyperuricemia?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fructose blocks the renal transporter required for urate excretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fructose directly activates xanthine oxidase in the liver

choices.label: C
choices.text: Fructose supplies the carbon skeleton for the purine ring

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fructose suppresses antidiuretic hormone, causing dehydration

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hepatic fructose metabolism rapidly consumes ATP, generating excess AMP

explanation.summary: Fructose is metabolized in the liver by an efficient enzyme that rapidly consumes ATP, producing excess AMP that feeds uric acid production.
explanation.whyCorrect: Consumption of high fructose corn syrup is a gout risk factor because fructose is uniquely metabolized in the liver through an efficient enzyme that rapidly consumes ATP. This leads to excess AMP, which is a substrate for uric acid production via the purine degradation pathway.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Interference with a uric acid excretion transporter is described for alcohol, not fructose.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Fructose does not act on xanthine oxidase; it raises the AMP substrate load.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The purine ring is built on carbon 1 of PRPP with contributions from glutamine and formyl-FH4; fructose is not described as a ring carbon source.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Inhibition of antidiuretic hormone leading to dehydration is a mechanism of alcohol, not fructose.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man with a history of gout drinks several beers every evening. Which of the following is a mechanism by which alcohol intake promotes his gout flares?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It blocks HGPRT in the salvage pathway, mimicking Lesch-Nyhan syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text: It enhances renal tubular excretion of uric acid, depleting the purine salvage pool

choices.label: C
choices.text: It increases PRPP synthetase activity in the liver, raising purine synthesis

choices.label: D
choices.text: It inhibits antidiuretic hormone, causing dehydration that concentrates urate

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inhibits xanthine oxidase, trapping hypoxanthine in the circulation

explanation.summary: Alcohol promotes gout by inhibiting ADH (dehydration), supplying purines (especially beer), and interfering with a uric acid excretion transporter.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alcohol intake is a common gout risk factor for three reasons: various spirits, especially beer, contain purines; alcohol inhibits antidiuretic hormone, leading to dehydration that raises urate concentration through lower solvent volume; and alcohol interferes with a transporter needed for uric acid excretion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HGPRT blockade is not a mechanism of alcohol; Lesch-Nyhan is a genetic HGPRT deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Alcohol interferes with a uric acid excretion transporter, reducing rather than enhancing excretion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Increased PRPP synthetase activity is not a described effect of alcohol.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xanthine oxidase inhibition (allopurinol's action) would lower uric acid and reduce, not promote, flares.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with long-standing hyperuricemia and firm tissue outgrowths on his ears and fingers develops severe flank pain. Imaging reveals a uric acid kidney stone. Which of the following urinary conditions most promotes formation of these stones?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acidic urine

choices.label: B
choices.text: Alkaline urine

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dilute urine

choices.label: D
choices.text: High urinary glutamine

choices.label: E
choices.text: High urinary orotic acid

explanation.summary: High circulating uric acid can crystallize as tophi in tissue and form kidney stones, especially when the urine is acidic.
explanation.whyCorrect: High levels of uric acid cause problems beyond the joint. Circulating uric acid can crystallize in tissue, causing outgrowths known as tophi, and uric acid crystals can form kidney stones especially when the urine is acidic.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Acidic, not alkaline, urine is the condition described as favoring uric acid stone formation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Dilute urine lowers urate concentration; dehydration and concentrated urine promote crystallization.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Glutamine is a nitrogen donor in nucleotide synthesis and has no described role in uric acid stone formation.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Orotic acid crystals appear in the urine of hereditary orotic aciduria, a pyrimidine disorder unrelated to uric acid stones.

questions.topicName: Nitrogenous Base Metabolism

questions.stem: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the dermatologist because he develops severe blistering sunburns after only a few minutes of sun exposure. Examination shows extensive freckling and several actinic keratoses on sun-exposed skin, and he has already had one squamous cell carcinoma removed. Which DNA repair pathway is most likely deficient in this child?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Base excision repair

choices.label: B
choices.text: Homologous recombination

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mismatch repair

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nonhomologous end joining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nucleotide excision repair

explanation.summary: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair, leaving UV-induced pyrimidine dimers unrepaired.
explanation.whyCorrect: UV light produces helix-distorting pyrimidine dimers that are corrected in humans by nucleotide excision repair (NER). Deficient NER activity causes xeroderma pigmentosum, marked by extreme photosensitivity, severe sunburn from brief exposure, and a greatly increased risk of skin cancer from accumulated unrepaired UV damage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Base excision repair corrects single altered bases such as uracil or oxidized bases, not the bulky pyrimidine dimers caused by UV light.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Homologous recombination repairs double-strand breaks; its loss (e.g., BRCA mutation) predisposes to breast and ovarian cancer rather than xeroderma pigmentosum.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mismatch repair corrects base-base mismatches from replication errors; its deficiency causes Lynch syndrome, not photosensitivity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nonhomologous end joining repairs double-strand breaks; its defects cause SCID or ataxia-telangiectasia, not the photosensitive skin-cancer phenotype described.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A researcher irradiates cultured skin cells with ultraviolet light and then examines the DNA for structural changes. Which of the following lesions is most characteristic of this exposure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A double-strand break severing both strands of the double helix

choices.label: B
choices.text: Addition of a methyl group to the O6 position of a guanine residue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Covalent bonding between adjacent pyrimidines on the same strand

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deamination of a cytosine base to uracil within the strand

choices.label: E
choices.text: Loss of a purine base leaving an abasic site in the backbone

explanation.summary: UV light causes neighboring pyrimidines to form abnormal covalent bonds, creating pyrimidine (thymine) dimers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Within a DNA strand, adjacent pyrimidine bases absorb UV light and form abnormal covalent bonds called pyrimidine dimers (mainly cyclobutane thymine dimers). Because the neighboring pyrimidines bond to each other rather than to their complementary bases, the helix is distorted and kinked, interfering with transcription and replication.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Double-strand breaks are characteristic of ionizing radiation such as X-rays, not UV light.
whyWrongByChoice.B: O6-methylguanine results from methylation/alkylation, an endogenous chemical modification, not from UV light.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Deamination of cytosine to uracil is a spontaneous endogenous event repaired by base excision repair, unrelated to UV exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Depurination, which produces an abasic site, is an endogenous hydrolytic lesion repaired by base excision repair, not a UV-specific injury.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman is diagnosed with colorectal cancer. Her family history is notable for colorectal and endometrial cancers occurring in multiple relatives before age 50. Genetic testing reveals a germline mutation in MSH2. A defect in which of the following processes best explains her cancer predisposition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Correction of base mismatches introduced during replication

choices.label: B
choices.text: Direct repair of alkylated bases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Excision of oxidized single bases

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rejoining of double-strand breaks by homologous recombination

choices.label: E
choices.text: Repair of UV-induced pyrimidine dimers

explanation.summary: Lynch syndrome arises from germline mutation in a mismatch repair gene, impairing correction of replication errors.
explanation.whyCorrect: MSH2 is one of the four mismatch repair (MMR) genes (with MLH1, MSH6, and PMS2). A germline mutation causes Lynch syndrome (hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer), in which uncorrected replication mismatches accumulate. Affected individuals have markedly increased, often early-onset, colorectal and endometrial cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct repair (e.g., MGMT) removes methyl groups; it is not the MMR pathway affected by MSH2 mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excision of oxidized single bases is base excision repair, a different pathway from the mismatch repair encoded by MSH2.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homologous recombination repairs double-strand breaks; BRCA (not MSH2) defects impair it and predispose to breast and ovarian cancer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Pyrimidine dimer repair is performed by nucleotide excision repair, whose loss causes xeroderma pigmentosum, not Lynch syndrome.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: During replication, a uracil residue is mistakenly incorporated into a strand of DNA. In the base excision repair pathway that corrects this error, which enzyme performs the first step by recognizing the abnormal base and removing it to create an apurinic/apyrimidinic site?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DNA glycosylase

choices.label: B
choices.text: DNA ligase

choices.label: C
choices.text: DNA polymerase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Helicase

choices.label: E
choices.text: Photolyase

explanation.summary: Base excision repair begins when a DNA glycosylase excises the damaged base to form an AP site.
explanation.whyCorrect: To initiate BER, a DNA glycosylase recognizes a damaged or incorrect nucleotide (such as uracil) and removes its base, creating an AP (apurinic/apyrimidinic) site. An endonuclease then cleaves the 5' phosphodiester bond and a lyase cleaves the 3' bond, after which DNA polymerase fills the gap and ligase seals the nicks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: DNA ligase acts at the end of the pathway, sealing the nicks after the gap is filled, not in recognizing or removing the base.
whyWrongByChoice.C: DNA polymerase fills the single-nucleotide gap after the AP site is processed; it does not create the AP site.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Helicase unwinds DNA (used in nucleotide excision repair to remove the segment) and does not excise the damaged base in BER.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Photolyase breaks pyrimidine dimers via photoreactivation and is absent in humans; it plays no role in base excision repair.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A cell sustains spontaneous methylation producing O6-methylguanine. Humans correct this lesion using a direct repair mechanism. Which of the following best describes how this repair is accomplished?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A glycosylase removes the base to form an AP site

choices.label: B
choices.text: A homologous chromosome is used as a template to restore the sequence

choices.label: C
choices.text: A stretch of nucleotides containing the lesion is excised and resynthesized

choices.label: D
choices.text: Photolyase uses light energy to reverse the modification

choices.label: E
choices.text: The enzyme MGMT removes the anomalous methyl group

explanation.summary: Direct repair by O6-methylguanine methyltransferase (MGMT) reverses methylation without cutting the DNA backbone.
explanation.whyCorrect: Direct repair corrects damaged bases without severing the phosphodiester bonds that hold nucleotides together. Humans use the enzyme O6-methylguanine methyltransferase (MGMT) to detect and remove anomalous methyl groups, directly reversing the lesion.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Glycosylase-mediated base removal to form an AP site is the first step of base excision repair, which severs the backbone, unlike direct repair.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Template-directed repair using a homologous chromosome is homologous recombination, used for double-strand breaks.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Excising and resynthesizing a stretch of nucleotides describes nucleotide excision repair, which does break the backbone, not direct repair.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Photolyase performs photoreactivation of pyrimidine dimers but is not present in humans and does not address methylation.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman is found to carry an inherited BRCA1 mutation that impairs the machinery normally used to accurately repair double-strand breaks using a homologous chromosome as a template. For which of the following is she at greatest increased risk later in life?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ataxia-telangiectasia

choices.label: B
choices.text: Breast and ovarian cancer

choices.label: C
choices.text: Squamous cell lung cancer

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lynch syndrome colorectal cancer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Xeroderma pigmentosum

explanation.summary: BRCA1/BRCA2 support homologous recombination; their loss markedly raises breast and ovarian cancer risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: BRCA1 and BRCA2 play crucial roles in homologous recombination repair of double-strand breaks (BRCA2 regulates RAD51). Mutations impair accurate repair and genomic stability, significantly increasing the risk of breast and ovarian cancer.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Ataxia-telangiectasia is associated with ATM and defective double-strand break signaling/nonhomologous end joining, not with BRCA-driven homologous recombination.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Lung cancer is linked to tobacco-smoke carcinogens and receptor gene polymorphisms, not to inherited BRCA-mediated homologous recombination defects.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Lynch syndrome is caused by mismatch repair gene mutations, not BRCA mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Xeroderma pigmentosum results from defective nucleotide excision repair, not from BRCA-associated homologous recombination defects.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: Of the DNA repair mechanisms, which is most likely to introduce a mutation into a cell's genome because it can join any two severed strands without requiring homology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Base excision repair

choices.label: B
choices.text: Homologous recombination

choices.label: C
choices.text: MGMT direct repair

choices.label: D
choices.text: Nonhomologous end joining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Nucleotide excision repair

explanation.summary: Nonhomologous end joining is error-prone because it fuses DNA ends without a homologous template.
explanation.whyCorrect: NHEJ uses a ligase complex to directly fuse the ends of two DNA fragments. Because it connects any two severed strands it can find and does not require homology, it is error-prone and can introduce mutations; when breaks occur on separate chromosomes it can cause translocations.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Base excision repair faithfully removes and replaces a single damaged base and is not a major source of mutation.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Homologous recombination uses a homologous chromosome as a template, so it reconnects strands without loss of sequence and is not error-prone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MGMT direct repair simply removes a methyl group without altering the sequence and does not introduce mutations.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Nucleotide excision repair accurately removes and replaces a lesion-containing oligonucleotide using the intact strand as a template.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A patient with epithelial ovarian cancer is treated with cisplatin. At the molecular level, which of the following best describes how this platinum-based drug damages tumor DNA to produce its antitumor effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It deaminates cytosine residues to uracil

choices.label: B
choices.text: It directly cleaves both strands to create double-strand breaks

choices.label: C
choices.text: It forms covalent adducts at the N7 position of guanine

choices.label: D
choices.text: It generates cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers between adjacent thymines

choices.label: E
choices.text: It inserts uracil into DNA during replication

explanation.summary: Platinum drugs covalently bind N7 of guanine, forming DNA crosslinks that drive their antitumor activity.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cisplatin and carboplatin interact with DNA to form mono-adducts, mostly covalently at the N7 of guanine. This mono-adduct then evolves into intrastrand crosslinks (the most abundant platinum adducts) or interstrand crosslinks, and the interstrand crosslinks are responsible for the antitumor activity.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Deamination of cytosine to uracil is a spontaneous endogenous lesion, unrelated to platinum drug chemistry.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Direct double-strand cleavage is characteristic of ionizing radiation, not of platinum adduct formation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers are produced by UV light, not by platinum chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uracil incorporation during replication is a replication/hydrolysis-related lesion repaired by base excision repair, not a platinum drug mechanism.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A cell's mitochondrial electron transport chain and a Fenton reaction generate a molecule with an unpaired electron that oxidizes DNA bases and can sever phosphodiester bonds. Which of the following is this reactive species?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hydroxyl radical

choices.label: B
choices.text: Molecular oxygen

choices.label: C
choices.text: O6-methylguanine

choices.label: D
choices.text: Thymine dimer

choices.label: E
choices.text: Uracil

explanation.summary: Hydroxyl radicals are reactive oxygen species with unpaired electrons that damage DNA in multiple ways.
explanation.whyCorrect: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) arise from endogenous sources such as the mitochondrial electron transport chain and Fenton reactions. The hydroxyl radical is a ROS produced from the reduction of hydrogen peroxide; because ROS have unpaired electrons, they are highly reactive and damage DNA by altering nucleotides, crosslinking strands, or severing phosphodiester bonds to cause strand breaks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Molecular oxygen becomes reactive only after gaining an extra electron (forming superoxide); stable O2 itself is not the damaging radical described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: O6-methylguanine is a methylated base produced by alkylation, not an oxygen radical.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A thymine dimer is a UV-induced DNA lesion, not a reactive oxygen species.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Uracil is a base that can be mistakenly incorporated into DNA; it is a lesion, not a reactive radical.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A 4-year-old child presents with progressive gait ataxia, choreic movements, and dilated blood vessels visible in the conjunctivae. Workup reveals a mutation affecting a gene that, through the MRN complex, is activated in response to double-strand breaks and coordinates their repair. Which gene is most likely mutated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ATM

choices.label: B
choices.text: BRCA2

choices.label: C
choices.text: MGMT

choices.label: D
choices.text: MLH1

choices.label: E
choices.text: XPA

explanation.summary: Ataxia-telangiectasia results from ATM mutation, impairing the double-strand break response downstream of the MRN complex.
explanation.whyCorrect: The proteins MRE11, RAD50, and NBS1 form the MRN complex in response to DNA damage and then activate ATM, the gene responsible for ataxia-telangiectasia. Affected children develop ataxia, chorea, myoclonus, and neuropathy usually before age 5, along with telangiectasias in the skin and eyes; NHEJ/double-strand break repair defects underlie this disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.B: BRCA2 regulates RAD51 in homologous recombination; mutations predispose to breast and ovarian cancer, not the neurologic phenotype described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MGMT performs direct repair of methylated guanine and is not activated by the MRN complex or linked to ataxia-telangiectasia.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MLH1 is a mismatch repair gene; its mutation causes Lynch syndrome, not ataxia-telangiectasia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: XPA is a nucleotide excision repair gene; its loss causes xeroderma pigmentosum with photosensitivity, not ataxia and telangiectasias.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: Nucleotide excision repair is especially important in humans for correcting UV-induced pyrimidine dimers. Which of the following best explains why humans rely so heavily on this pathway for these lesions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Humans cannot perform base excision repair

choices.label: B
choices.text: Humans have no DNA polymerase with proofreading capability

choices.label: C
choices.text: Humans lack functional photolyase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Humans repair pyrimidine dimers only by nonhomologous end joining

choices.label: E
choices.text: Humans use MGMT to reverse pyrimidine dimers directly

explanation.summary: Because humans lack photolyase, nucleotide excision repair is the key mechanism for repairing pyrimidine dimers.
explanation.whyCorrect: Photolyase is an enzyme that breaks pyrimidine dimers through photoreactivation using light energy, but bacteria, fungi, plants, and some animals have it while humans do not. Because humans lack photolyase, nucleotide excision repair (which occurs primarily in G1) becomes the important mechanism for repairing UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Humans do perform base excision repair; it simply targets single altered bases rather than bulky pyrimidine dimers.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Human DNA polymerases do have proofreading ability; this is unrelated to reliance on NER for dimers.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nonhomologous end joining repairs double-strand breaks, not pyrimidine dimers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MGMT reverses O6-methylguanine, not pyrimidine dimers, so it cannot explain reliance on NER.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: An oncology team notes that both cigarette smoke and platinum chemotherapy damage DNA. Which statement most accurately reflects a mechanism described for tobacco smoke as a source of DNA damage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It exclusively causes pyrimidine dimers in the lung epithelium

choices.label: B
choices.text: It induces aldehyde-driven DNA adducts and also reduces DNA repair

choices.label: C
choices.text: It protects the lung genome from carcinogens and enhances repair

choices.label: D
choices.text: It repairs double-strand breaks in the lung by homologous recombination

choices.label: E
choices.text: It reverses methylation of guanine residues at the O6 position

explanation.summary: Tobacco smoke forms aldehyde-driven DNA adducts and simultaneously impairs DNA repair, compounding damage.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tobacco smoke contains at least 70 carcinogens and induces acrolein- and crotonaldehyde-DNA adducts in the lungs, with aldehydes being the major driving force of the damage. Importantly, in addition to causing damage, tobacco smoke also reduces DNA repair, so damage that could otherwise be repaired is left uncorrected.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Pyrimidine dimers are caused by UV light; tobacco smoke acts mainly through aldehyde-DNA adducts, not exclusively dimers.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tobacco smoke damages the lung genome and reduces repair; it does not protect against carcinogens.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homologous recombination is a cellular repair pathway; tobacco smoke damages DNA rather than repairing double-strand breaks.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reversing methylation of guanine is the function of MGMT direct repair, not an action of tobacco smoke.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A population of cultured fibroblasts is exposed to a high dose of a mutagen. At the checkpoint preceding S phase, the cells halt division and attempt repair, but the amount of damage sustained is far too great for repair to be feasible. Which of the following is the most likely fate of these cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activation of programmed cell death (apoptosis)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Conversion of every lesion into a stable heritable mutation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Global demethylation of the genome by MGMT

choices.label: D
choices.text: Progression into S phase with replication of the damaged template

choices.label: E
choices.text: Removal of all lesions by photoreactivation

explanation.summary: When DNA damage is too extensive to repair, cell-cycle checkpoints trigger apoptosis rather than allowing division.
explanation.whyCorrect: Tightly regulated checkpoints exist in all replicating cells, especially before and after S phase. Cells halt division if a high level of damage is detected and attempt repair; however, if too much damage has been sustained and repair is not feasible, special mechanisms for apoptosis (programmed cell death) are activated to protect genomic stability.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A lesion becomes a mutation only if it is left uncorrected and the cell survives to replicate; the checkpoint response to overwhelming damage is death, not fixation of every lesion.
whyWrongByChoice.C: MGMT removes anomalous methyl groups from individual guanines; it does not perform global demethylation and is not a checkpoint response.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The purpose of the checkpoint is to prevent progression into S phase while heavy damage persists, not to allow replication of a damaged template.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Photoreactivation is performed by photolyase, which humans do not possess, and it addresses only pyrimidine dimers.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A researcher is cataloguing the sources of the roughly 70,000 DNA lesions each hepatocyte sustains per day. Which of the following is best classified as an endogenous source of DNA damage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Carcinogens inhaled from tobacco smoke

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hydrolysis of DNA strands during metabolism

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ionizing radiation from indoor radon gas

choices.label: D
choices.text: Platinum-based crosslinking chemotherapy agents

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ultraviolet light from midday sunlight

explanation.summary: Endogenous DNA damage arises from unintended consequences of the cell's own metabolic processes.
explanation.whyCorrect: Sources of genetic damage fall into two broad categories. Endogenous sources involve unintended consequences of metabolic processes, such as oxidation, nitrosylation, or hydrolysis of DNA strands; errors in DNA replication are another endogenous source. Exogenous sources are influences from the physical environment.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Tobacco smoke carcinogens are exogenous chemical exposures, not products of the cell's own metabolism.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Radon gas is a natural source of ionizing radiation, which is an exogenous influence from the environment.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Platinum drugs are exogenous crosslinking agents administered as chemotherapy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: UV light is an exogenous environmental influence and a particularly potent exogenous source of DNA damage.

questions.topicName: DNA Damage and DNA Repair Mechanism

questions.stem: A 3-year-old girl with microcephaly, recurrent infections, and progressive ataxia undergoes genetic testing that confirms Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome.
